items.s: Coleman did not catch his only target in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday. Coleman played 10 offensive snaps in Sunday's win. The fifth-round rookie participated in just 15 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays, taking a backseat to third-round rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas.

items.h: Kevin Coleman Jr. hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.s: Kevin Coleman Jr. hauled in 3-of-7 targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. The rookie made his mark in Sunday's loss to the Bengals. He caught three passes over the course of the afternoon, one of which he was able to turn into a touchdown. He isn't likely to be a good fantasy option moving forward, but he could continue to be an involved member of this offense for as long as Caleb Douglas (ankle) remains out of the lineup.

Coleman caught three of seven targets for 30 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Bengals. Coleman finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wide receiver Malik Washington (eight). Coleman's most significant moment in Week 5 came in the fourth quarter when he reeled in a three-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Malik Willis. Coleman has now caught five of 17 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown over five contests this season.

items.h: Kevin Coleman Jr. Playing as Dolphins' Third Receiver
items.s: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. has established himself as the team's third receiver for as long as Caleb Douglas (ankle) is sidelined. Last week, Coleman played 51% of snaps against the Vikings, more than double the combined total of veterans Ryan Miller and Jalen Tolbert. Coleman only caught one pass for three yards, but he did rank second on the team in targets with four. The rookie from Missouri will likely remain in the role behind Malik Washington and Chris Bell, and he does bring some flier upside since he's getting playing time. Last week, QB Malik Willis only managed nine complete passes and 85 passing yards, so there hasn't been much production to go around. In…

items.h: Kevin Coleman Jr. Could Get More Work in Minnesota
items.s: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. has been on the field regularly over the last two weeks, although the fifth-round rookie from Missouri has yet to make much of an impact. He played 46% of snaps in Week 2 and saw that increase to 62% of snaps in Week 3 with Caleb Douglas (ankle) out. Without Douglas, Coleman served as the Dolphins' third receiver behind Malik Washington and Chris Bell, but he only managed one catch for three yards on four targets. He only had two targets and no catches in the first two weeks of the season, so without Douglas, he did get a big boost in involvement. Douglas is out again in Week 4 against the Vikings, which should lead to Coleman getting good…

items.h: Kevin Coleman Jr. catches one pass in Week 3
items.s: Kevin Coleman Jr. caught one of his four targets for three yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 3. Coleman Jr. has been minimally involved in the Miami offense to begin the season, recording a catch for the first time in three contests. The wideout remains one of many underwhelming options in a dismal Dolphins offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

Coleman played 27 offensive snaps and saw no targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers. Coleman played 46 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps in the blowout loss. The fifth-round rookie appears to have taken a backseat to Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas (ankle) and Chris Bell. Coleman could see an uptick in usage in the team's Week 3 game against the Chiefs if Douglas cannot play due to his ankle injury.

items.h: Held without catch in NFL debut
items.s: Coleman failed to bring in his two targets during Sunday's 27-13 loss to Las Vegas. Malik Willis missed on both of his pass attempts to Coleman late in the fourth quarter. Coleman's 16 snaps on offense were fourth-most among Dolphins wide receivers, and the rookie fifth-rounder figures to operate in a rotational role on offense behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. Coleman will look to record his first NFL catch in a Week 2 tilt against the 49ers on Sept. 20.

items.h: Kevin Coleman Jr. sees two targets in Week 1
items.s: Kevin Coleman Jr. failed to catch either of his two targets in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1. Coleman Jr. was one of many minimally involved in the Miami passing attack in the season opener, finishing only ahead of Will Kacmarek in targets. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats until further notice ahead of a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

items.h: Team's leading receiver in preseason loss
items.s: Coleman (undisclosed) caught two of five targets for 32 yards in Saturday's 26-3 preseason loss to the Giants. Coleman had previously dealt with an undisclosed injury that caused him to miss some practice time, but the rookie fifth-round pick suited up Saturday and paced the team in targets and receiving yards. The Dolphins rested their starters and got an ugly passing performance out of the backups, as Coleman was the only player on the team to exceed 12 receiving yards in the game. Coleman seems to be running well behind rookie third-round pick Caleb Douglas, as well as the more experienced Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell. items.h: Coleman missed Friday's practice due to an undisclosed injury, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.s: The rookie sixth-round pick doesn't seem to have made much noise early on at training camp, while third-round pick Caleb Douglas reportedly was one of the standouts at Friday's session. There's still time for Coleman to make his case for a role this summer if the injury he's dealing with doesn't turn out to be serious.

items.h: The Dolphins selected Coleman in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 177th overall.
items.s: Coleman played for four different schools during his four-year college career, which ended in 2025 with Missouri, when he posted 66 catches for 732 yards and one touchdown across 13 games. He served primarily as a slot wide receiver and had the explosiveness to beat the first man, and his experience as a punt returner could earn him playing time in his rookie season in the NFL. Coleman is the third wide receiver selected by the Dolphins in this year's draft, joining Texas Tech's Caleb Douglas and Louisville's Chris Bell.
